records.words: A practical question: why the lantern goes dark. I like that, sounds like a fault to trace.
Works on the table, dies when carried. My electrician guess: loose connection that opens with movement. I will reproduce it first, like at work.
Fault reproduced. Before I open anything I switch it off, habit from work.
A real circuit: cell pack, switch, contact, bulb, nodes A to D. I suspect the contact first, it is the part that moves when carried.
Contact is aged and dull - a suspect, but looks are not proof. The guide wants me to measure from the battery outward while carrying. Proper method, I approve.
Voltage needs power, so I switch it back on for the measurement.
6.00 V while carried, battery is healthy. Guide says switch next, but I want across the contact first - if it opens, the full 6 V shows across it. My own order.

0.00 V across the contact. So either the contact is fine or no voltage even reaches C - the break is upstream. My aged-contact theory is weaker. The guide was right to point at the switch. B to C now.
6.00 V across the switch while carried - it opens when moved. Exactly how I would find it at work. Satisfying. The dull contact was a red herring.
Clean, adjust, replace. Only one spare switch, so I will not spend it blindly. Look first - 10 min is cheap.

A real tradeoff: my only new switch, or strip the cracked spare lantern which may give a useless part. Guide says replace. I try adjust first - costs only time, keeps the spare. If it fails I learn something.

Adjust did not help, still goes out. Fair, I can explain that: mounting was not the problem, the switch inside is. 35 min lost, but I learned. The guide wants me to measure the battery again - why? I already know. I spend the new switch.

Fixed in under a minute of real time. Reproduce, measure battery, measure across parts while carried, switch shows 6 V, adjust failed, replace worked. That is real fault-finding, I enjoyed it. I used my only new switch, and I wonder if that will cost me later. Tappable: power switch, carry, look inside, parts, meter probes and conditions, repair actions, notes. The day bar and £24 at top are the limits.
Family favour, £0. Fine, it was Sam's mother. But my only switch is gone for nothing. Now the workshop opens up: Bench, Board, People.

Now the planning game. Three jobs, all due Day 2 17:00, none examined, so I promise blind. I have about 1.5 workdays. I take two, not three: the fan pays most, the reading light is like the lantern I just fixed. I will skip the music box unless time is left.
Three identical Accept buttons, I pick the fan one by position.
Now the reading light.
My tap at 376 missed, the layout moved up after the fan left the column. Tapping where the button actually is.
Fan first, it pays most. A bit fiddly finding it: everything stacks in one narrow column and the right half of the screen is empty.
Same circuit shape, motor instead of bulb. Test is work harder with filter fitted. Reproduce first.
Weak under load. My guess: a high-resistance joint eating voltage when current rises, or a tired battery. Meter under load will tell.
Meter condition still on Carry from the lantern - I nearly missed that. Switching to work harder.
Motor gets only 1.49 V under load. So the motor is starved, the loss is before it. 4.5 V is going somewhere. Contact next.
C to 0 this time: if C is near 6 V, the contact eats it.
C is 1.51 V too. Contact is innocent, wrong again. Loss is at the switch or the battery itself sags. Battery under load next.
The black probe was active, not the red. I have to pick which probe I am moving.

Battery itself only 1.54 V under load. Dead cells. I should have measured the battery first, like the guide taught me on the lantern - I went downstream first and spent 20 minutes. My mistake, I can explain it.
Again only one in stock. If Nora's reading light also needs a cell I am stuck, but the fan pays £32 against £18. I spend it here. Worry noted: I have no visible way to buy parts yet.
Steady air. Back to Rafi. I never looked at the filter the request mentioned - I hope that does not bite me.
£32 in, now £56. Rafi works at a dish station in Bornova - Izmir, close to home, I smiled at that. Reading light next. No cells, no switches left in stock though.

Two jobs done, money up from 24 to 56, and each fault I could explain with the meter. I like it. The only friction is hunting buttons in one long column, and the worry that my part stock is now empty.
Reading light, same 4-part circuit. Reproduce first.
Dim under load, same symptom family as the fan. Lesson learned: battery first this time. If it is the battery I have no cell left - that would hurt.
Battery 5.91 V, healthy. Relief - I do not need a cell. Now what reaches the bulb.
C still 5.88 V. Switch is fine. So the contact or the bulb. D next.
D only 3.21 V. 2.7 V lost across the contact under load. Finally the contact IS guilty this time - a corroded joint. Clean costs no part. Perfect.
Bright and steady. Clean worked, no part spent. Best repair of the day - measured, fixed cheaply.
£74 now. Three for three. I still have 2 hours and a whole Day 2, so the music box is affordable in time. Accepting it.
A mechanical one: spring, gear, governor, drum, target 15 ± 3 turns per minute. Outside my trade, but the same chain logic. Play it first.
Meter switches to motion mode for mechanical things. Clever. Source first again: the spring.
-150.00 turns per minute (difference)? Negative, difference from what? A to 0 should be the spring output. I had to read it twice. It tells me to compare with Notes.

Now I have a ratio sheet: spring 150, gear /5 = 30, governor x ring, drum /2. Ring 2 gives 15. Proper calculation, I like it. The spring shows 150 in size - the minus sign I guess is probe direction, not sure. Check the gear output next, should be 30.

Wait - maybe -150 difference means 150 below the rating, so the spring shaft is not turning at all? But the drum barely turns, not stopped. I really do not know which reading it is. Measure B and compare.

B reads -7.50, "this shaft turns slowly". So the minus is direction and the numbers are speeds: spring 150 ok, after gear should be 30, is 7.5. The gear is slipping. Clear now - I was confused by the word difference for two readings.
Look before spending my one gear. On the lantern I wasted adjust; looking first is cheaper.

"The outside looks intact" - same words as the switch, it tells me nothing. 10 minutes for nothing. I have 90 minutes left today: adjust and test fits, and replace still fits after if needed. Try adjust.
Same speed after adjust. Second time adjusting wastes 35 min - I should learn that adjust rarely helps here. Replace the gear, should finish by 16:50.
Melody keeps its pace. 16:50 - returning lands right at 17:00. Tight, but a whole Day 2 job done on Day 1.

Ouch. "I do not want new parts; I want this one to work." It was her grandmother's box. I never saw that request before I replaced the gear - on the lantern the owner's words showed on the bench, here I only saw the Play instructions. Maybe it was behind the ▾ name button. I feel bad, and a bit cheated: I would have tried clean first. Still paid £26, now £100.

Ouch. "I do not want new parts; I want this one to work." It was her grandmother's box. I never saw that request before I replaced the gear - on the lantern the owner's words showed on the bench, here I only saw the Play instructions. Maybe it was behind the ▾ name button. I feel bad, and a bit cheated: I would have tried clean first. Still paid £26, now £100.
Requested layout check, not my own choice.
Phone check: the board actually reads better on phone - cards are compact, buttons beside the title, Wait and Close at the bottom. Nothing cut off that I saw. Back to desktop.
Day is used up. Close. I want to see what Day 2 brings and whether I can buy parts - my stock of switch, cell and gear is all gone.
Day 2, no new requests on the board. Empty Asked-of-you column. Maybe People shows who might bring work.

Here is the shop I was missing: parts £4 to £18, a second bench £48, a tester £35. Now £100 means something - real tradeoffs. Also I see Nora's no-new-parts request was written here all along; I missed it. And Sam asked to watch me on Day 1 and I ignored him. Two things I can fix today.

The tester for harder use says compare readings while it works harder - but I already measured under work harder yesterday. Why would I buy that? Confusing, I skip it. Instead I ask Sam to watch; he wanted that on Day 1 and I ignored him. Then I will open the cracked spare lantern - the title asks why the lantern goes dark.
Sam is watching. The cracked spare lantern, same circuit as Sam's mother's. I will do it properly this time: reproduce, battery first, walk down the chain.
Meter remembers the last condition (work harder) again - I have to remember to switch it. Carry.
0 V across the switch - not the switch this time (unless battery is dead). Contact C-D next, it is the cracked one maybe.
B to D now spans switch and contact together. Fine, it still tells me something.
0 V across switch and contact. So either the bulb opens or the battery is dead. Across the bulb next.
Both probes on D now, silly. Moving black to 0.

6.00 V across the bulb while carried - the bulb opens when moved. Same symptom as Sam's mother's lantern, different part! That is a nice lesson: symptom does not equal cause. I have one bulb in stock.

Wait. On the cracked spare lantern the repair tab only offers Look closely and Recover part. No clean, adjust or replace. So it is not a repair, it is a parts donor? I spent 45 game minutes and Sam's lesson diagnosing something I am not allowed to fix. Nobody told me that before I opened it. Mildly annoyed. I do not know what Sam learns from this now.
Look closely at the bulb, maybe it tells me why I cannot replace it.
Outside looks intact again, same as the gear. Look closely never tells me anything. I check the board for new work.
More on the lantern card. Maybe it says what I can do with it.

OK, the card explains it: casing ruined, it is a parts donor. That was written here, I just never opened More. Fair. So the lesson was diagnosis practice and a free bulb source? The bulb is the broken part though, so recovering it is useless. Switch and cell are good, I could recover those. Now the paper theatre, unexamined.
Paper theatre has a music note icon, so probably the mechanical kind. Open it.
Target 12 plus minus 1 turns per minute when working harder. Clear. Play it first.
Too fast. My guess is the governor, it is the part that should slow it. But I measure first, I learned that with the gear.
Meter remembered Carry from the lantern again. Switch to work harder.
Red at C, after the governor, black at ground. Should show how fast the governor output turns.
-48 at C. Negative again, I still do not love the minus sign. Check notes for the normal speed.

Now I like this. 150 divided by 5 is 30 at B. I need 12 at the drum, so 24 out of the governor, so ring setting 1, times 0.8. I read 48, that is times 1.6, setting 4. If B is really 30 the ring is just turned too far and Adjust should fix it without a new part. Good, no new parts this time. I check B before I trust it.
Black still on 0, red on B now. Read.

B is 30, as I calculated. So the governor ring is wrong, and the little 4 on the governor icon was the setting all along. I did not notice it was the ring number until now. Sam left right at the end of the measurement; he kept what he saw. Adjust governor.
Ring is set to 4, a real dial with 0 to 4. I pick 1 from my calculation.
Skip the extra measurement, I trust the math. Straight to the test.

Best moment so far. I did the arithmetic from the notes, predicted setting 1, measured B to confirm, set the ring, and it passed first time. No part spent, no owner upset. This is exactly the kind of thing I enjoy: a visible reason and my own plan.
Both projects are mine, no paying work. I do not know what my projects are for, there is no money for them. Wait half an hour for a customer.
Nobody came. Check People, maybe someone asks there.
Sam's list now has the steps he watched, written very mechanically. Repairs alone: 0. Maybe that is the real goal, to get him to do one alone. I ask him.

Sam talks about copying another player's bug report and the developer. That is strange inside a repair shop, it pulled me out of the workshop for a second. Is this game about playtesting? I do not know. No paying work, no requests. I close the day and see if day 3 brings customers.

Recognition, before checking anything: Halil, 61, a repairman working fewer hours, planning to call his daughter Selin. That is the Halil from the Voice game, where I told him to call Selin and see the doctor. Visible cue: name Halil plus daughter Selin plus repairs. Confidence: fairly high that it is meant to be him, but it stays a guess. My reaction: oh, Halil! Nice to see him somewhere he can just bring a lantern. Also: money went from 100 to 96 overnight and nothing told me why. Rent? I do not like an unexplained loss.
Maybe the day button explains the 4 pounds.
The day sheet says nothing about the 4 pounds. Unexplained, I leave it. Go take Halil's lantern.
Suddenly four requests at once, after a whole empty morning yesterday. And a community afternoon. Feast or famine.
Meeting-room fan, 24 pounds, accept. Fans I know: check the cell under work harder.
Sam's winding toy, 22. Accept.
Halil's lantern, 20. Of course I accept.
The community fan pays nothing but Sam's mother asks and it is for the community afternoon, I think. Accept it, I have two days.
Bench opened the community fan, the earliest one. Fine, do it first.
Voltage at the motor under load first. If it is full 6 the motor is bad, if low I walk back up the chain.
Motor gets 1.69 V. Now the battery itself.

Battery dead again, 1.76 V. No cell in the drawer. But the cracked spare lantern had a good battery, 6.00 V. Recover it: 25 minutes and free, versus 6 pounds and 20 minutes to buy. Now the parts donor makes sense. I like this tradeoff.
Recover the good battery.
The object list sheet does not scroll and the community fan is off the bottom. I go round by the board instead. A bit of fiddling.

What? Replace says No cell stocked. I just spent 25 minutes recovering the cell from the cracked lantern and it said You finished recovering the part. Where did it go? This is exactly the kind of loss I hate. I check the drawer.

Drawer says cell 0 in stock. The recovered battery just disappeared, 25 game minutes and a whole spare lantern for nothing that I can see. Plus 4 pounds gone overnight with no reason. I made a good plan and the game ate it without telling me why. I want to stop here. I will buy a cell and finish the fan and Halil's lantern, then see.
Fine, buy a cell for 6 pounds.
Fan works. Return it.
Done. Now Halil.
Halil's lantern. Same symptom as Sam's mother's lantern: dark when carried.
Straight to the bulb while carried. If 6 V, the bulb is bad and I have one bulb in stock.

The diagnosis itself still holds me, I can walk the chain with the meter and that feels like real work. But the vanished battery and the 4 pounds still bother me, and moving between objects is fiddly. Halil's bulb has 0 V, so the break is upstream. Middle of the road now.
B 6 V, C 0 V: the switch opens when carried. Same fault as the very first lantern. No switch in the drawer. Adjust failed last time, but I try once before paying 9 pounds.

Adjusting the switch did nothing, the light still goes out while carried. Twenty minutes for a fix that was never going to work - the meter said switch, but not that adjusting cannot fix it. I will buy a switch for nine pounds.
Steady while carried. The new switch did it; adjusting was a wasted twenty minutes but I can explain it. Returning to Halil.
Same symptom as the community fan. I will measure the battery first this time.
Battery low again, 1.54 V. Now I know the pattern: fans come in with weak cells. Buy a cell, six pounds, fitting cost is clear.
Second fan, same fault, fixed in under a minute of my time. £119 now. It feels good but also a bit like a routine: test, meter A to 0, buy cell, replace. Only the winding toy is left.
I tapped the wrong card - the page was a different height than I thought. Second try on the winding toy.

The toy is a proper puzzle again: spring reads 31.5 slow against 90, and even with a good spring the ring at 2 gives 15, so I need ring 3 for 18. Two faults, I can see both on paper. This is what I like.
Not enough time to set the ring today - fair, it is 16:45 and the day ends at 17. It said so clearly. I close the day and finish the toy tomorrow morning; it is due Day 4 17:00.

107 became 103 overnight again. Four pounds every night and still nothing tells me what for - rent? I can guess but I do not like guessing about money. The community afternoon is now open: three activities, my theatre could be used. Interesting, but first the toy.
Passed first try. My arithmetic was right: new spring plus ring 3. That is the satisfying kind of repair.
My own theatre on the stage - that is a nice use for the thing I fixed. Nothing else to repair, so I wait for the site to open.
Everyone chose my paper theatre - all five. Including Halil. I am pleased, honestly.
All five came and watched the theatre I repaired. That closes the circle nicely. I close the day to see if there is more.
Day 5, minus four pounds again, no new requests on the board. I wait once to see if anyone brings work.
Every job is returned, the theatre show went well, and now the board is empty and the money just drips four pounds a night. I have nothing to plan. This is a good place to leave.

I am stopping on Day 5 with every promise kept and the paper theatre shown to all five neighbours. The meter puzzles - the governor sums, the spring and ring together - were the best part, and I could explain every setback except the four pounds that vanish each night and the recovered cell that never reached the drawer. Now the board is empty. I would return voluntarily another evening if new objects arrive with puzzles like the theatre and the toy; I would not come back just to repeat the battery swap on fans. I would not leave it running. Feedback: I selected I am stopping, typed nothing, submitted nothing.
